entry.label: Soft Systems Methodology (SSM)
entry.description: Soft Systems Methodology is a participative learning process for messy, contested human situations. It uses rich pictures, purposeful activity models and structured comparison to support inquiry and feasible change.

profile.title: Soft Systems Methodology (SSM)
profile.canonical_definition: Soft Systems Methodology is a participative learning process for messy, contested human situations. It uses rich pictures, purposeful activity models and structured comparison to support inquiry and feasible change.
profile.summary: Soft Systems Methodology is a learning-oriented process for inquiring into messy situations through rich pictures, explicit worldviews, purposeful activity models and structured comparison.
profile.why_it_matters: SSM separates systemic inquiry from the claim that the situation itself is one objectively specifiable system. It is designed for plural purposes and contested improvement.
key_distinctions: model as inquiry device vs model of reality
common_misreadings: SSM is a fixed seven-step recipe
profile.editorial_note: Developed from public primary, institutional and publisher sources. Open to correction, rival interpretation and stronger evidence.
